title: Why You Zone Out During Simple Tasks: The Brain's Default Mode
hook: Why does your mind wander during routine chores?

narration.text: Your brain has a special network that activates when you are not focused on a task.
This is called the Default Mode Network, or DMN.
It helps us remember the past, plan the future, and understand others.
When you are doing something easy, like washing dishes, your DMN takes over.
This is why you suddenly realise you have been daydreaming for minutes.
It is not a sign of poor focus; it is your brain being efficient.
So, next time you are spacing out, remember your brain is working hard.
Have you noticed your mind wandering during simple activities?

description: Ever found yourself zoning out while doing something mundane? It is not just you. Your brain's Default Mode Network is likely the reason. Discover how this amazing neural system works to help you think about more than just the task at hand.
topic: Why you sometimes 'space out' during routine tasks, explaining the brain's default mode network.
